newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee slips sharply to end at 35.79/80 a dlr.
newsitem.headline: India rupee slips sharply to end at 35.79/80 a dlr.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.79/80 per dollar on Wednesday, sharply weaker from an opening rate of 35.73, dealers said.
A leading Calcutta-based bank hit the market soon after opening, pulling down the rupee to a low of 35.81, they said.
The Calcutta bank bought dollar hungrily soon after the open, buying at 35.74 to 35.77 levels.
The rupee stabilised around these levels until the bank hit again, chasing the rupee to 35.7950/8050 per dollar, dealers said.
Desperate covering by some Bombay banks, who were surprised by rupee's steep fall, pushed the rupee down to the day's low of 35.81 per dollar, dealers said.
Fresh dollar supplies at this stage caused the rupee to edge up to 35.79/80 level towards the close. The Calcutta bank hit the market a third time, mopping up dollars at this level.
"But there was no panic among importers," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay. "Everyone knew it's one bank that hit the market."
Most dealers said the Calcutta bank was buying dollars for state-run companies, mainly to pay for India's oil imports.
"The overall trend is clear," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "The rupee may see 35.85/90 level in the coming weeks."
Many dealers said the Reserve Bank of India appeared to be happy with the rupee's depreciation as long as it was gentle.
Premia on the forward dollar spurted on the back of rising overnight call rates, dealers said. Call closed at 10.50 percent after opening the day at 7.50 percent, dealers said.
The six month annualised premium closed at 7.32 percent, up from the previous close of 6.54 percent, dealers said.
